messages:
maria: heads up — after the kernel-scheduler bump we're seeing Mixtral MoE p50 token latency jump and clear expert hotspots.
kevin: saw the alert. can you paste numbers?
maria: p50 went 18ms -> 42ms, throughput down ~32%. GPU profiles show a small set of experts burning 6-8x more cycles than baseline. quick profiler snippet: 
```text
hotspot_experts: [12, 47, 12, 12]
kernel_time_per_token_ms: 0.9 -> 3.8
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.87 -> 0.54
```
jordan: hmm — did we change router logit smoothing or the top-k default in the last deploy?
maria: the scheduler PR introduced logit clipping for stability and bumped topk default for the canary to 32 to reduce rejection. i suspect higher fanout -> kv thrash.
sophia: yup, more topk increases fanout and KV pressure. did anyone try lowering topk?
kevin: ran a quick sim on the same trace: topk 16 -> 8 reduced avg_experts_per_step 2.9 -> 1.8 and p99 tail improved notably. eval quality delta was tiny on our prompt set.
maria: idea: instead of hard-lowering topk, try a softcap that prunes low-prob experts. keep k high but apply min-prob threshold. prototype patch below.
jordan: paste the patch or a snippet please.
maria: ```diff
router.py +37
- routed = topk_logits(logits, k=16)
+ routed = topk_with_softcap(logits, k=16, prob_thresh=0.12)
```
sophia: also consider increasing expert_parallelism (replicating an expert across 2 shards) to reduce per-expert kernel queueing hotspots. caveat: more parallelism can raise KV memory and cross-device comms.
kevin: exactly — doubling parallelism cuts per-expert queueing but increases KV shard count and might worsen cache pressure unless we also shard KV or increase per-device cache memory.
maria: proposed A/B/C canary plan: 
- A) baseline canary (current patch)
- B) topk 8 + kernel scheduler unchanged
- C) topk 16 + softcap(prob_thresh=0.12) + expert_parallel=2 + kv_shard_per_device
we'll measure p50/p99, throughput, kv_hit_rate, and eval perplexity on the regression prompt set.
jordan: add a kernel-selection axis too: use int8 kernels for cold experts (lower mem) and fp16 for hot experts (better throughput) — scheduler picks per-expert kernel based on recent ROI.
sophia: i'll add a tiny probe to emit per-expert kernel_selection_count and kv_liveness_histogram so we can correlate selection to thrash.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job 1918202760 for runs A/B/C on canary pool (8 instances) — results ETA ~45m
kevin: one more thing — RoPE scaling impact: on long-context traces router entropy increases and we observed avg_experts +40% for contexts >8k. include RoPE-length stratified eval in the plan.
maria: good catch. will add stratified buckets (<=2k, 2k-8k, >8k).
sophia: if results look good we should roll softcap + kernel-selection heuristics as opt-in for dedicated customers first; we can push aggressive defaults after more canaries.
maria: agreed. i'll run the checklist and post results when perf-bot finishes :thumbsup:
